geographical_area: City of Catania and most of its province (urban Catanese). The profile follows the city norm; the Etna sub-varieties (CT I-IV in the Vocabolario siciliano) and the adjoining Siracusa area are not described separately. Palermitano and western Sicilian, Messinese and the metaphonetic varieties of central and south-eastern Sicily are excluded.
linguistic_classification: Sicilian (Siciliano), Extreme Southern Italo-Romance, eastern non-metaphonetic group, Catanese variety; traditionally called a dialect, also classed as a regional language.
language_family: Indo-European > Romance > Italo-Romance > Extreme Southern Italian (Sicilian)
orthographic_conventions: Popular phonetic spelling: final vowels only -a, -i, -u; dd for the retroflex from Latin -LL- (beddu, iddu; alternative ḍḍ); articles u, a, i; j for /j/ (jornu); gghi (figghiu); chi- from pl- (chianu); apostrophes for aphaeresis ('mbari, 'nzirtari); circumflex contractions (ô, â, dû, hâ, âmu). At intensity 4-5 the Catanese changes are written (r assimilated before consonants: fotti, jonnu; d > r: rumani, ranni from granni); at 1-2 the general Sicilian spelling is used (forti, jornu, dumani, granni).
description_en: Catanese Sicilian: three-vowel unstressed system (-a, -i, -u), no metaphonic diphthongs, retroflex dd, rhotacism of d (rumani), assimilation of preconsonantal r (fotti, jonnu), full infinitives (-ari, -iri), passato remoto as the everyday past, no productive future (present + adverb or aviri a + infinitive), aviri a for obligation, stari + gerund for the progressive, accusative a with animate objects, subjunctive in place of the conditional and 3pl -unu endings (diciunu). Voice: a friendly, ironic speaker who calls everyone 'mbari and urges with 'avaia!'.
description_it: Il siciliano di Catania: vocali atone solo -a, -i, -u, nessun dittongo metafonetico, dd cacuminale, rotacismo di d (rumani), assimilazione di r davanti a consonante (fotti, jonnu), infiniti interi (-ari, -iri), passato remoto come passato di tutti i giorni, nessun futuro produttivo (presente + avverbio o aviri a + infinito), aviri a per il dovere, stari + gerundio per il progressivo, a davanti a complemento oggetto animato, congiuntivo al posto del condizionale e terza plurale in -unu (diciunu). Tono: amichevole e ironico, chiama tutti 'mbari e sprona con 'avaia!'.

identifier_word.meaning_en: Sicilian vocative 'mate, buddy', from Latin compater (godfather, companion).
identifier_word.meaning_it: Vocativo siciliano 'amico, compare', dal latino compater (compare).
identifier_word.attestation: Wiktionary lists 'mbari and notes it is often written 'mbare; Martoglio's Centona (Catania, 1899) writes 'mpari; SoloLibri places 'mpare/'mbare in the north-east (Catania, Messina) versus compà/cumpà in the south-west. The mode name is the popular spelling 'mbare, not the academic form 'mbari.

known_limitations: No native-speaker review yet: all example sentences are AI-illustrative, built on documented rules.
Catanese-specific forms rest mainly on Martoglio's Centona (1899) and on Wikipedia pages; modern spoken Catanese may differ (e.g. -unu 3pl, 2pl -stru/-stuu).
Sicilian spelling is not standardized (dd/ḍḍ, u/'u/lu, j/i): the profile picks one form and lists alternatives; intensity 1-2 uses general Sicilian spelling.
Several colloquial and vulgar items rest on low-reliability popular or journalistic sources and are marked accordingly in the data files.
No Catanese blasphemous formula was found in the sources, so none is documented or generated.
Palermitano and Catanese differ (e.g. pacchiuni, compà vs 'mbari, preconsonantal r): items attested only for the west were excluded, but gaps may remain.
